slides.title: Chemical Reactions and Equations
slides.speaker_notes: Welcome to chemistry's foundation: how to write, balance, and classify reactions.

slides.title: What you'll be able to do
bullets: Spot indicators of a chemical reaction.
Convert word equations to chemical equations.

slides.title: When has a reaction happened?
bullets: Any of these = chemical reaction LIKELY.

slides.title: Law of Conservation of Mass
bullets: Atoms are NEVER created or destroyed.
Same atoms on both sides → BALANCED equation.

slides.title: Balance: 3 Fe + 4 H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4 H₂
bullets: Step 3: 4 O from 4 H₂O = 4 O in Fe₃O₄.

slides.title: Reaction types — 1 to 3
bullets: 1. COMBINATION: A + B → AB. (e.g. 2 Mg + O₂ → 2 MgO)
2. DECOMPOSITION: AB → A + B. (e.g. 2 H₂O₂ → 2 H₂O + O₂)
3. DISPLACEMENT: A + BC → AC + B. (e.g. Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu)
More reactive metal displaces less reactive.
Reactivity series tells you what works.

slides.title: Reaction types — 4 and 5
bullets: 4. DOUBLE DISPLACEMENT: AB + CD → AD + CB.
Oxidation = gain of O / loss of H.
Reduction = loss of O / gain of H.

slides.title: Decomposition — three sub-types
bullets: THERMAL — driven by heat. (CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂)
PHOTOCHEMICAL — driven by light. (2 AgCl → 2 Ag + Cl₂)
ELECTROLYTIC — driven by electricity. (electrolysis of water)
Energy must be supplied to break things apart.

slides.title: Redox example: CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O
bullets: Both happen at the same time.

slides.title: Corrosion in everyday life
bullets: Rusting needs BOTH oxygen and moisture.

slides.title: Rancidity — oxidation in food
bullets: Oils / fats slowly oxidise → bad smell, taste.

bullets: 3. In CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, what is oxidised?
4. Why is silver chloride stored in dark bottles?
5. Two methods to prevent rust on a bicycle.

bullets: Q1. What does Δ above the arrow mean?

slides.title: Key takeaways
bullets: 5 types: combination / decomposition / displacement / double displacement / redox.
Oxidation = gain of O; reduction = loss of O.
Corrosion + rancidity = oxidation in everyday life; prevent with barriers and antioxidants.
